name: JK Tyre & Industries Ltd
title: JK Tyre & Industries Ltd - 530007 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Supply-side expansion of ~Rs 4,980 cr for TBR/PCR (+24% capacity) on top of Rs 1,130 cr already underway, with utilisation above 90% and price hikes of 4-5% taken, with 5-6% more planned against an 18-20% raw material cost rise.

utilisation.quote: Installed capacities were fully utilized across segments and for the full year at India level, the utilization was recorded at above 90%.

capex.quote: the Board, in addition to the expansion projects of Rs.1,130 crore under implementation, has approved to undertake further brownfield expansions for PCR and TBR segments at an aggregate cost of Rs.4,980 Cr in phases until 2029.

triggers.label: Capacity +24% via Rs 4,980 cr expansion
triggers.quote: This will increase TBR & PCR capacities by 24%

triggers.label: Price hikes 4-5% taken, 5-6% more
triggers.quote: We have already taken a hike of 4-5% across products in replacement market and 5 -7% in export markets.

triggers.label: Peers matching price hikes
triggers.quote: the competition has also taken price hikes, and I would say they are also in the same range as what we have taken.

triggers.label: Off-highway player entering TBR/PCR
triggers.quote: one of the off-highway players has announced big plans over the next few years with respect to TBR, PCR and two wheeler.

triggers.label: Q4 domestic volumes +21%
triggers.quote: Domestic markets recorded a healthy volumes growth of 21%, led by a robust 42% growth in OE Market.

guidance.metric: Raw material cost Q1FY27 vs Q4
guidance.quote: raw material prices are expected to go up by 18 -20% in Q1FY27 from Q4.
This will increase TBR & PCR capacities by 24%
Total cash outlay on yearly basis would be roughly around Rs.1,200 crores
this Rs.1,130 crores will get completed by Q3 of FY28.

red_flags.label: Mexico sluggish growth; US tariffs
red_flags.quote: Our Mexican subsidiary did witness a little sluggish growth this quarter. This was mainly due to the heightened geopolitical volatility and trade uncertainty owing to US tariffs.

red_flags.label: Debt rising to fund expansion
red_flags.quote: Consolidated debt as on 31.03.26 stood at Rs.4,445 crores vis-à-vis Rs.4,081 crores as on 31.03.25

red_flags.label: Price hikes may hurt demand
red_flags.quote: I think a peer had highlighted that there could be some demand moderation because of the price hikes that are being taken

evasions.topic: Peer demand moderation from price hikes
evasions.quote: going forward, actually, it will be depending on the war, but we are seeing some softening to an extent in the crude oil prices.

evasions.topic: Funding mix of Rs 6,110 cr capex
evasions.quote: the total amount of outlay also includes the loans which we will take.

summary.headline: JK Tyre Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 42% YoY to Rs.546 crore on 12.9% margin, with a further Rs.4,980 crore brownfield expansion approved.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs.4,233 crore and PAT rose 83% to Rs.188 crore, with FY26 revenue at a record Rs.16,384 crore. Management said volume growth was broad-based, led by domestic OE and TBR, and margin expansion came from volumes, mix and cost control. Raw material costs are expected to rise 18-20% in Q1 FY27, which management is offsetting with staggered price hikes of 4-5% (replacement) and 5-7% (export), with a further 5-6% under way. The Board approved Rs.4,980 crore of additional PCR and TBR brownfield capacity to 2029, on top of the Rs.1,130 crore already under implementation.

segments.name: Consolidated mix Q4 FY26 (by revenue)
segments.commentary: Truck & bus ~56%, PLR ~27%, non-truck bias ~13%, 2/3W ~4%. Market split: replacement 63%, OE 27%, exports ~10%.

segments.name: Standalone mix Q4 FY26
segments.commentary: Truck & bus 59%, PLR 25%, non-truck bias 12%, 2/3W 5%. Standalone replacement 61%, OE 30%.

segments.name: JK Tornel (Mexico)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs.2,138 crore (FY25: Rs.2,147 crore); FY26 EBITDA Rs.141 crore, PBT Rs.61 crore (+63%), PAT Rs.42 crore (+91%). Q4 revenue Rs.378 crore, EBITDA Rs.24 crore (+36% YoY); management described Q4 as sluggish on US tariff uncertainty.

segments.name: Domestic India volumes
segments.commentary: Q4 domestic volumes +21% YoY; OE +42%. TBR replacement +19%, TBR OE +53%. Passenger line +16% (replacement +10%, OE +26%). Farm volumes +58% (replacement +30%, OE nearly doubled, exports +44%). 2/3W OE +72%, 2/3W exports +31%.

segments.name: Exports (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 export volumes steady; FY26 export volumes +5%. Passenger exports +20% for FY26. Premium 16-inch+ domestic sales +13% in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Raw material prices expected to rise 18-20% in Q1 FY27 vs Q4 FY26 (CFO-level figure stated as 18-19% later in Q&A); management sees some softening in crude and possible raw material relief from Q3 FY27 if conditions hold.
Further price hike of 5-6% under way on top of 4-5% already taken in replacement (5-7% in exports); OEM price increases lag. Mainly taken in Q1 FY27.
Management expects demand to remain buoyant in FY27, with mid-single-digit growth in some categories; no OEM order cuts seen.
Cash outlay of about Rs.1,200 crore per year; total expansion of Rs.6,110 crore (Rs.1,130 crore + Rs.4,980 crore) to complete by FY29, with debt-to-equity of about 2:1 on the projects.
Rs.1,130 crore expansion to complete by Q3 FY28; capacity for TBR and PCR to rise 24%.
capex_capacity: Installed capacities fully utilised across segments; India utilisation above 90% for FY26.
Rs.1,130 crore expansion under implementation (mainly TBR, some PCR), completion by Q3 FY28.
Board approved further brownfield PCR and TBR expansion of Rs.4,980 crore in phases until 2029, increasing TBR and PCR capacity by 24%.
Management stated the Rs.4,980 crore plan is in addition to the Rs.1,130 crore; the total of Rs.6,110 crore is to be spent over three to four years.
2/3W: growth via productivity improvements and expanded outsourcing of 2/3W tyres.
demand_pricing: Q4 price hikes of 4-5% in replacement and 5-7% in export; OEM pricing lags. Competitors have taken hikes in the same range, per management.
Management reports no OEM order book cuts across CV, passenger or other lines, though supply chains were disrupted by the West Asia crisis.
New OEM approvals in FY26 from Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland, Mahindra, Switch Mobility, VECV and Euler Motors; 50+ new brand shops added.
Management cited the Levitas Ultra premium passenger offering, puncture guard and smart tyres, and the 'selling miles' fleet mobility programme as barriers to entry against new entrants.
Management noted a peer's warning on possible demand moderation from price hikes, but did not give a view on Q2/H2 demand impact.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 market and category mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated: replacement 63%, OE 27%, exports ~10%. Truck & bus ~56%, PLR ~27%, non-truck bias ~13%, 2/3W ~4%. Standalone: truck & bus 59%, PLR 25%, replacement 61%, OE 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Mexico (JK Tornel) decline QoQ, and was there an impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mexico was sluggish in Q4 due to geopolitical volatility and US tariff uncertainty. FY26 revenue was steady at Rs.2,138 crore vs Rs.2,147 crore. No impairment was mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the price hike came in Q4 vs Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly in Q1 FY27. OEM price increases lag, and a further 5-6% hike is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded, and what is the FY27 outlay?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash outlay of ~Rs.1,200 crore per year. Debt will be taken, supported by higher EBITDA; project funding is about 2:1 debt-to-equity. Leverage expected to stay comfortable at 2-3 year levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus funds from the Dec-2023 QIP, held in fixed deposits, have been gradually withdrawn and deployed into expansion projects, reducing interest income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook and order book position?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand expected to stay buoyant in FY27, with strong or mid-single-digit growth in some categories. No OEM order cuts seen.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.5,000 crore capex in addition to the Rs.1,130 crore, and when does the Rs.1,130 crore finish?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the new plan is in addition. The Rs.1,130 crore is under implementation and will complete by Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material outlook for Q1 and Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material costs are rising ~18-19% in Q1 FY27. Some softening in crude is expected, which could ease raw material costs beyond Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How has competition responded to price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Competitors have taken price hikes in the same range (about 4-5%).

qa_highlights.question: How will JK Tyre defend its position against new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an entrenched OEM and fleet position, premium products, the selling miles fleet programme, and OEM technical norms in passenger cars.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for 2/3W and off-highway?
qa_highlights.answer: 2/3W growth via productivity gains and outsourcing, with more outsourcing planned. No specific off-highway plan was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Rs.6,000 crore outlay over 3-4 years be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. FY26 cash generation exceeded Rs.1,600 crore; the outlay includes planned borrowings and internal accruals. Spending can rise if needed.

risks_watch: Raw material costs guided up 18-20% (CFO 18-19%) in Q1 FY27; margin sustainability depends on speed and size of price hikes (4-5% taken, further 5-6% under way) and OEM lag effects

Execution and funding of Rs.6,110 crore expansion (Rs.1,130 crore to Q3 FY28; Rs.4,980 crore in phases to FY29) at ~Rs.1,200 crore annual cash outlay, with debt-to-equity about 2:1 on projects; net debt/EBITDA is 2.13x at 31-Mar-26
Mexico (JK Tornel) Q4 slowdown tied to US tariff uncertainty; Q4 revenue Rs.378 crore; USMCA review due July 2026
Competitive entry: management mentioned a large off-highway player's plans in TBR, PCR and 2/3W; peer warned of possible demand moderation from price hikes, with no management view on Q2/H2 impact
West Asia crisis supply disruptions and rupee weakness; management hopes for US-Iran peace talks to normalise energy markets by H2 FY27
key_quotes: Keeping in view the ongoing situation, raw material prices are expected to go up by 18 -20% in Q1FY27 from Q4.
We have not seen any order books getting cut from any of the OEM, be CV s, passenger or any other line.
So, these total expansions of Rs.6,110 crores will be completed by FY29.
Yes, the Rs.5,000 crore worth of capex is in addition to Rs.1,130 crore expansion plan.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and FY26 delivery, with a record year and a Rs.4,980 crore expansion approval. Cautious on input costs and geopolitics: management said the West Asia crisis is pressuring margins and gave no view on Q2/H2 demand impact from price hikes. Evasive on the Mexico Q4 decline, attributing it to tariff uncertainty without quantifying it.

adds.what: Rs.1,130 cr TBR and PCR brownfield expansion (mainly TBR, some PCR) under implementation
Rs.4,980 cr additional brownfield PCR and TBR expansion in phases until 2029, lifting TBR and PCR capacity by 24%

growth.why: Management expects demand to stay buoyant in FY27 with mid-single-digit growth in some categories and no OEM order cuts, backed by a Rs.1,130 cr expansion due by Q3 FY28 and a Rs.4,980 cr approved brownfield plan adding 24% TBR/PCR capacity by FY29, though no specific FY27 revenue number was given and utilisation is above 90%.
